- When sentiment is high (≥0.6), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for low sentiment periods.
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% upward bias to initial forecast points.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- Model shows mean reversion bias: if price is above 65, forecast tends to drop; if below 60, tends to rise — adjust toward recent 7-day average if deviation >3%.
- Sentiment and price move in tandem: if sentiment rises >0.2 from prior day, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the final 3–5 days; apply a 1–2% upward bias to last 3–5 forecast points if sentiment is rising.
